subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust/provenance contract should OpenClaw support across memory-core, QMD/session memory, Active Memory, Memory Wiki bridges, and plugin SDK surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but trust assignment, persisted schema, config modes, plugin visibility, and retrieval enforcement define a security boundary and product contract that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Define native contract first
options.body: Keep #7707 open as the trust-policy tracker and specify framework-owned source/trust metadata, review state, expiration, and retrieval weighting before implementation.

options.title: Land provenance prerequisites first
options.body: Prioritize #42647/#48519/#28913-style source attribution and capture filtering, then layer trust tiers and policy enforcement once provenance is durable.

options.title: Externalize advanced trust stores
options.body: Document world-model-mcp/AKF-style tools as optional integrations for now while leaving default OpenClaw memory behavior unchanged until a missing core API is approved.

recommendation.title: Define native contract first
recommendation.body: Keep #7707 open as the trust-policy tracker and specify framework-owned source/trust metadata, review state, expiration, and retrieval weighting before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined signal from the prior #7707 review and memory host/core policy history.
